examples.en: Value-added tax is a typical indirect tax.
Indirect taxes are included in the price of goods.
The share of indirect taxes is rising.
I didn't know that consumers pay indirect taxes.
Indirect taxes apply the same regardless of income.
In social studies we learned about direct and indirect taxes.

explain: 물건을 살 때 값에 섞여 내는 세금이라서, 소득에서 바로 내는 '직접세'와 짝으로 배워요. 대표적인 예가 부가가치세예요. 뉴스나 경제 수업에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I learned the difference between direct and indirect taxes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대 개념인 '직접세'와 짝으로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said as a pair with its opposite, 직접세 (direct tax).

phrases.en: I pay indirect tax every time I buy something.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 낸다는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you pay the tax.

phrases.en: Indirect tax is included in the price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값 안에 세금이 들어 있다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that the tax is already inside the price.

explain_en: It is a tax built into the price when you buy something, so it is learned as a pair with '직접세' (direct tax), which is paid straight from income. VAT is the typical example. It often appears in the news and economics classes.

examples.en: If a majority agrees at the meeting, the proposal passes.

examples.ko: 열두 명 중 일곱 명이면 과반이에요.
examples.en: Seven out of twelve people is a majority.

examples.ko: 이번 투표에서 어느 후보도 과반을 얻지 못했어요.
examples.en: No candidate won a majority in this vote.
More than half of the students in the class agreed to the picnic.
A majority is different from unanimity, where everyone agrees.

examples.ko: 표가 과반에 못 미쳐서 다시 투표해요.
examples.en: The votes fell short of a majority, so we are voting again.

explain: '과반'은 딱 절반이 아니라 절반을 넘는 것이고, 보통 '과반수'라고 많이 말해요. '가장 많은 표'와는 달라서, 후보가 셋 이상이면 1등이어도 과반이 아닐 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The majority agreed, so it was decided.
phrases.nuance_ko: '과반'보다 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More commonly used in daily life than 'gwaban'.

phrases.en: The votes in favor exceeded the majority.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절반보다 많아졌다는 뜻으로 투표 이야기에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means going past half, often used for votes.

phrases.en: That candidate failed to win a majority of votes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선거에서 절반이 넘는 표를 얻는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Winning more than half the votes in an election.

explain_en: '과반' means more than half, not exactly half, and people often say '과반수'. It differs from 'the most votes': with three or more candidates, the winner may still not have a majority.

examples.en: Many people on Jeju Island make a living from tourism.

examples.ko: 관광업은 날씨와 경제 상황에 영향을 많이 받아요.
examples.en: The tourism industry is greatly affected by weather and the economy.

examples.ko: 관광객이 늘면서 관광업이 다시 살아나고 있어요.
examples.en: As tourists increase, the tourism industry is recovering.
I studied the tourism industry in college.
To work in tourism, it helps to be good at foreign languages.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 관광업 덕분에 다시 활기가 생겼어요.
examples.en: This village regained its energy thanks to tourism.

explain: '관광'은 구경하며 여행하는 것이고, '관광업'은 그걸로 돈을 버는 산업이에요. 같은 '-업' 말로 '농업', '서비스업'이 있어요.

phrases.en: This city has a well-developed tourism industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고 뉴스나 설명하는 글에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, often used in news and explanatory writing.

phrases.en: My older sister works in the tourism industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업이나 일하는 분야를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone's job or field.

phrases.en: Fewer travelers have come, so the tourism business is struggling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기가 좋지 않을 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when business conditions are poor.

explain_en: '관광' is traveling to see sights, while '관광업' is the industry that earns money from it. Other '-업' words include '농업' (agriculture) and '서비스업' (service industry).

examples.en: This year, the economic slowdown was clearly visible.
Voices worried about the slowing growth are getting louder.

examples.ko: 소비 둔화에도 불구하고 온라인 판매는 꾸준히 늘었어요.
examples.en: Despite the slowdown in spending, online sales kept growing.

examples.ko: 금리가 오르면 경기 둔화로 이어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If interest rates rise, it can lead to an economic slowdown.

examples.ko: 인구 증가 둔화는 사회에도 큰 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: The slowdown in population growth has a big impact on society too.
The news analyzed the causes of the export slowdown.

explain: 경제 뉴스에서 '성장 둔화', '경기 둔화', '소비 둔화'처럼 많이 나와요. 완전히 멈추는 게 아니라 늘어나는 속도가 줄어든다는 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '가속'이에요.

phrases.en: Sales at the shop fell because of the slowdown in spending.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 쓰는 돈이 늘어나는 속도가 느려질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the growth of consumer spending slows down.

phrases.en: A slowdown in the economy is a concern.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 걱정하는 마음을 나타낼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news to express worry.

phrases.example: 인구 증가의 둔화 현상이 나타나고 있어요.
phrases.en: A slowdown in population growth is appearing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 변화가 눈에 띄게 나타날 때 '현상'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 현상 points to a noticeable change.

explain_en: It appears often in economic news, as in '성장 둔화', '경기 둔화' and '소비 둔화'. It does not mean stopping completely but the pace of growth decreasing. The opposite is '가속'.

examples.en: This country has a relatively high illiteracy rate.
The government built schools to lower the illiteracy rate.
Illiteracy rates differ greatly from country to country.
I saw global illiteracy rate statistics on the news.
As education expanded, the illiteracy rate dropped a lot.
The results of the illiteracy survey were announced today.

explain: '문맹률이 높다/낮다', '문맹률을 낮추다'처럼 써요. 교육 수준을 이야기하는 뉴스나 수업에서 많이 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: Korea has a very low illiteracy rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라의 교육 수준을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a country's education level.

phrases.en: The illiteracy rate went down thanks to education.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 지나며 변하는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a change over time.

phrases.en: The government did a survey of the illiteracy rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 보고서에서 자주 보이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in news and reports.

explain_en: It is used like '문맹률이 높다/낮다' and '문맹률을 낮추다'. You will often meet it in news and classes that discuss education levels.

examples.en: The amount of waste generated is growing every year.

examples.ko: 이 공장은 먼지 발생량을 줄이려고 노력해요.
examples.en: This factory is trying to reduce the amount of dust it produces.
The amount generated varies by season.
The results of the survey on the amount generated were announced today.
If you cut down on packaging, the amount of plastic waste goes down too.

examples.ko: 집집마다 쓰레기 발생량에 따라 봉투 값을 내요.
examples.en: Each household pays for bags according to how much waste it produces.

explain: 쓰레기, 먼지, 이산화탄소처럼 '나오는 양'을 말할 때 써요. 환경 뉴스에 자주 나오고 '늘다, 줄이다, 감소하다'와 함께 써요. 비율은 '발생률'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My neighborhood produces a lot of waste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경 뉴스에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in environment news.

phrases.en: Food waste increases in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나오는 양이 많아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount grows.

phrases.en: If you cut packaging, the amount goes down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나오는 양이 적어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount decreases.

explain_en: Used for the amount of things that come out, like waste, dust or carbon dioxide. It often appears in environmental news with verbs such as 늘다, 줄이다 and 감소하다. The ratio is called '발생률'.

en: poor people; the poor; the needy

examples.ko: 도시 빈민층을 돕는 단체에서 자원봉사를 해요.
examples.en: I volunteer at an organization that helps the urban poor.
They provide free meals to children from poor families.

examples.ko: 이 정책은 빈민층의 생활을 안정시키는 게 목표예요.
examples.en: The goal of this policy is to stabilize the lives of the poor.

examples.ko: 빈민층이 사는 지역에 새 학교가 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new school opened in the area where poor people live.

examples.ko: 빈민층에 속한 가정은 의료비 부담이 커요.
examples.en: Families in the lower-income class carry a heavy burden of medical costs.

examples.ko: 신문에서 빈민층은 해마다 늘고 있다는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article in the paper saying the number of poor people is growing every year.

explain: 사회 계층을 말할 때 쓰는 말로, 뉴스나 사회 수업에서 자주 나와요. 반대말은 '부유층'이에요. 사람을 직접 '빈민'이라고 부르면 거칠게 들릴 수 있어서, 뉴스에서는 '저소득층', '취약계층' 같은 말도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Housing is a big problem for the urban poor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사회 문제를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about social issues.

phrases.en: Helping low-income families is important.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빈민층'보다 부드럽고 뉴스에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 빈민층 and more common in the news.

phrases.en: This organization helps the poor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '을'을 붙여 도움을 주는 활동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 을, it describes helping activities.

explain_en: It is used when talking about social classes and often shows up in the news and social studies. Its opposite is '부유층'. Calling a person '빈민' directly can sound harsh, so the news also uses words like '저소득층' and '취약계층'.

examples.en: My father went to reserve forces training today.
A man who has finished the army becomes a reservist.
I took a day off because of reserve training.
People in reserve-forces uniforms got on the bus.

examples.ko: 동네 예비군 부대가 학교 옆에 있어요.
examples.en: The local reserve forces unit is next to the school.

examples.ko: 예비군은 몇 년 동안 훈련을 받아요.
examples.en: Reservists receive training for several years.

explain: 군대를 마친 한국 남자가 일정 기간 받는 훈련을 '예비군 훈련'이라고 해요. 남자들이 '예비군 간다'처럼 아주 일상적으로 말해요. 여자는 대상이 아니라서 친구나 아버지 이야기에 주로 나와요.

phrases.example: 남편은 다음 주에 예비군 훈련을 받아요.
phrases.en: My husband will have reserve forces training next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation.

phrases.example: 친구는 내일 예비군 가서 못 만나요.
phrases.en: My friend has reserve training tomorrow, so we can't meet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남자들이 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual expression men use in conversation.

phrases.en: My father went out wearing his reserve forces uniform.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훈련 때 입는 옷을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The uniform worn during the training.

explain_en: Korean men who have finished the army must attend '예비군 훈련' for a set period. Men casually say '예비군 간다' for it. Women are not subject to it, so it mostly comes up in talk about a friend or father.

examples.en: This company holds 30 percent of the market.

examples.ko: 큰 차가 주차 공간을 두 칸이나 점유했어요.
examples.en: A big car took up as many as two parking spaces.

examples.ko: 그 가족은 오랫동안 이 집을 점유해 왔어요.
examples.en: That family has occupied this house for a long time.

examples.ko: 자리를 점유하는 사람 때문에 다른 손님이 못 앉았어요.
examples.en: Because of a person hogging a seat, other customers couldn't sit down.

examples.ko: 인기 있는 상품이 매장 앞쪽을 점유할 거예요.
examples.en: The popular products will take over the front of the store.
You must not occupy a public place as you please.

explain: '차지하다'와 거의 비슷하지만 더 딱딱해서 뉴스, 서류, 법 이야기에 어울려요. 자리와 공간뿐 아니라 '시장의 30퍼센트를 점유하다'처럼 비율에도 써요. 목적어에 '을/를'을 붙여요.

phrases.en: The big sofa takes up half of the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하지만 더 부드러운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The meaning is similar, but this is softer and used in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 가방으로 빈 자리를 점유하면 다른 사람이 앉을 수 없어요.
phrases.en: If you occupy an empty seat with your bag, other people can't sit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리나 공간을 혼자 차지해서 쓰는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone takes a seat or space for their own use.

phrases.en: Please don't take up the hallway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 공간을 막지 말라고 공손하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices to politely ask people not to block a space.

explain_en: Close to 차지하다 (take up), but stiffer, so it fits news, documents and legal talk. It works for seats and spaces, and also for shares, as in 시장의 30퍼센트를 점유하다. The object takes 을/를.

examples.en: Many participating nations gather at the Olympics.

examples.ko: 이번 대회의 참가국은 모두 서른 나라예요.
examples.en: There are thirty participating countries in this tournament in total.
Each participating country has a different cheering culture, so it's fun.
The organizers announced the participating countries.
Korea is also included among the participating nations of this event.
Representatives of the participating countries gathered in the meeting room.

explain: 대회나 회의, 행사에 나오는 나라를 말할 때 써요. 대회를 여는 나라는 '개최국'이나 '주최국'이라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 뉴스와 스포츠 기사에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Many countries took part in this tournament.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참가국'을 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out way of saying 참가국.

phrases.en: The number of participating countries went up from last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회 크기를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe the size of an event.

phrases.en: The athletes from the participating countries entered one after another.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회에 나온 나라의 선수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for athletes from the countries in an event.

explain_en: Use it for the countries that take part in a competition, meeting or event. The country that hosts it is called '개최국' or '주최국', so it helps to learn them as a pair. You will often see it in news and sports articles.

examples.en: The farmers got together and formed a cooperative.

examples.ko: 우리 동네에는 주민이 운영하는 협동조합 가게가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a cooperative store run by residents in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 협동조합에 가입하면 싸게 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you join the cooperative, you can buy things cheaply.
A cooperative shares its profits among its members.
University students opened a cooperative cafe.

examples.ko: 그 우유는 낙농 협동조합에서 만든 거예요.
examples.en: That milk was made by a dairy cooperative.

explain: '협동조합'은 일반 회사와 달리 낸 돈의 크기가 아니라 사람 한 명이 한 표를 가져요. 농업 쪽은 '농협', 생활용품 쪽은 '생협'처럼 줄여서 부르는 일이 많아요. 가입한 사람은 '조합원'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I joined the local cooperative last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조합의 구성원이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when becoming a member of the cooperative.

phrases.en: I am a member of this cooperative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가입한 사람을 '조합원'이라고 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: People who joined are called '조합원'.

phrases.en: The residents run the cooperative themselves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조합을 맡아서 이끌어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when managing and running the cooperative.

explain_en: Unlike an ordinary company, a cooperative gives each person one vote regardless of how much they put in. Shortened names are common, such as '농협' for farming and '생협' for consumer goods. A member is called a '조합원'.
